pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis ( secondary to Ovarian Teratoma ) THE SMOKING GUN: Pelvic ultrasound revealing a 3.5 cm right ovarian mature cystic teratoma (dermoid cyst) containing ectopic neural tissue, alongside positive CSF IgG autoantibodies against the GluN1 subunit of the NMDA receptor. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Ectopic neural elements contained within the ovarian teratoma break immune tolerance and trigger systemic humoral immunity. Autoantibodies cross the blood-brain barrier and bind specifically to the GluN1 subunit of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors. This induces antibody-mediated receptor cross-linking and internalisation, dramatically decreasing functional cell-surface NMDA receptor density. The localized hypofunction of NMDA receptors disrupts inhibitory frontostriatal pathways, causing a predictable sequence of psychosis, catatonia, involuntary movements, autonomic dysfunction, and hypoventilation. Surgical excision of the teratoma combined with immunotherapy leads to full or substantial recovery in most cases.
